clue.text: Most spacious old semi collapsing amid decay

indicators.note: amid tells us the old-semi letters sit in the middle of the word for decay

parts.note: decay means rot

indicators.note: a collapsing house falls into disorder, so the letters of semi are rearranged

explanation.surface: An estate agent's description of a crumbling old semi-detached house as the most spacious on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi' looks like a house, and it is, but here its letters are the anagram fodder; 'amid' splits the word for decay around the old-semi letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means having plenty of space, so its superlative is a straight synonym for most spacious.

clue.text: Criminal ways of making money

definitions.meaning: The gentleman burglar of E. W. Hornung's stories
a raffle is a lottery held to raise funds

explanation.walkthrough: A.J. Raffles is a famous fictional gentleman thief; raffles are prize draws used by charities to raise funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Prize draws raise funds for charities, and the name belongs to a well-known fictional burglar.

clue.text: Covers Rover's paw, badly injured

indicators.note: something badly injured is left out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet bandages a dog named Rover after he hurt his paw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly injured' rearranges the letters of ROVERS PAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwrap something is to wrap it on the outside, which is to cover it.

clue.text: Terrible fire in plant when oxygen added

parts.note: a fern is a kind of plant
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A plant catches fire badly once oxygen feeds the flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when ... added' is only a link: the pieces simply follow on in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a huge raging blaze, so a terrible fire is a good synonym.

clue.text: In school control class — no girl may make loud noise

indicators.note: In places the school abbreviation round the rest

parts.note: to run a business is to control it

indicators.note: no tells us to take away the word for girl

parts.note: taken from the clue as written before removal
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A teacher fears a class without girls in it may turn noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class — no girl' leaves just the first letter C. 'control' reads as a noun, but it is the verb run, as in running a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrunch is a loud crunching sound, so to scrunch is to make that noise.

clue.text: Stock food item put, say, upon rolls

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
upon means on top of, atop

explanation.surface: A grocer stacks a stock item of food on top of bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' has no wordplay role; the blog's commenters complained that it spoils the grammar. 'rolls' looks like bread, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick soup, the sort of dish made from stock, sold as a food item.

clue.text: Noble comrade's final resting place

parts.note: a pal is a comrade, and the possessive gives the S
the grave is where one finally rests

explanation.surface: The burial site of a noble comrade.
explanation.walkthrough: A palsgrave is a German count palatine, a historical noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: A palsgrave was a German count with palatine powers, a noble rank.

clue.text: Cultivation of crops up to maturity

parts.note: till means up to, as in wait till morning
to come of age is to reach maturity

explanation.surface: Farming crops until they are fully ripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the preparing and working of land for growing crops.

clue.text: Money stuffed into empty grip by a family member

indicators.note: something stuffed into another goes inside it
an emptied word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Money crammed into a bag by a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves GP from GRIP; 'stuffed into' puts GRAND inside; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a member of the family, and this is the familiar name for him.

clue.text: Brawl in which no-one's laid out?

definitions.meaning: a brawl is a chaotic fight with everyone joining in
read literally, an event where nobody has laid out money, i.e. entry costs nothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' suggests knocked unconscious in a brawl, but here it means spent money: nobody pays.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly fight that anyone joins is called by this hyphenated phrase, and its words also describe something costing nothing.

clue.text: Unprofitable bank

definitions.meaning: a ... year is a poor, unproductive one
to bank is to tilt or incline, as an aircraft does in a turn

explanation.definitionFit: Lean means meagre or unrewarding, and as a verb it means to tilt sideways, which is what banking is.

clue.text: Terribly dangerous, when confronted by cow, to be caught napping?

indicators.note: being confronted by something means having it in front, so the cow word comes first

parts.note: a cow lows, so as a pun it is something that lows

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of dangerous are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a dangerous cow can catch you off guard while you doze.
explanation.walkthrough: A cow is a 'lower' because it lows (moos), a pun on the comparative of low. 'when confronted by' means the cow piece stands in front of the anagram of 'dangerous' signalled by 'Terribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxing your vigilance is exactly how you come to be caught napping, so the idiom fits with a question mark.

clue.text: Scotsman's cry of surprise after marine creature's seen … here?

definitions.text: Scotsman's cry of surprise after marine creature's seen … here?

indicators.note: after places the Scottish exclamation behind the creature

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal
och is a Scottish exclamation

explanation.surface: A Scot exclaims in surprise on spotting a seal, and we ask where this happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a Scot spotting a seal and saying 'Och!' is a scene you would find at a long Scottish sea inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea inlet in Scotland is exactly where a Scot might see a seal and exclaim in surprise.

clue.text: Concern to preserve distinctive feature in ornamental piece of architecture

indicators.note: preserving something holds it safely inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: care means concern
a touch is a characteristic mark, as in a personal touch

explanation.surface: Worry over keeping a distinctive detail on a decorative architectural piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to preserve' means the concern word holds the feature word inside it, split after its third letter. A cartouche is an oval or scroll-shaped decorative panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is a decorative scroll-shaped tablet or panel in architecture.

clue.text: What road builders do to advance

definitions.meaning: read literally, road builders construct a way, a route
to step aside for someone so they can advance or pass

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is looser: to give way lets someone else advance, or the phrase means to make progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally constructing a road, and idiomatically clearing room so progress can be made.

clue.text: You'll get richer while rate fluctuates

indicators.note: something that fluctuates shifts around, so the letters of while rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: An investor gets richer while the interest rate goes up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuates' rearranges the letters of WHILE RATE; 'You'll get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wealthier means having more money, a straight synonym for richer.

clue.text: Grazing land beyond river

parts.note: beyond means past, as in walking past a house
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Farmland for grazing lies on the far side of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of grass where livestock feed is the plain meaning of this farming word.

clue.text: In which females are gripped by a strong emotion?

definitions.text: In which females are gripped by a strong emotion?

indicators.note: something gripped is held inside, so the females go within the emotion phrase

parts.note: ire is anger, a strong emotion
FF is the plural abbreviation of female
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: A clue describing a love affair in which women are seized by passion.
explanation.walkthrough: An are is a metric unit of area (100 square metres), abbreviated A. 'gripped by' puts FF A inside A IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An affaire is a love affair, an episode in which passion grips those involved.

clue.text: One drinker beats another one up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to top is to beat or surpass
another drinker, a sot

explanation.surface: A drunkard beats up a fellow boozer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beats ... up' looks like an assault, but 'beats' gives the synonym and 'up' turns the whole charade round, as befits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a habitual heavy drinker.

clue.text: Compose small pieces for quintets

parts.note: to compose a letter is to pen it
tads are small amounts or bits

explanation.surface: A composer writes short pieces for groups of five musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quintets' looks like the music the pieces are written for, but it is the definition: groups of five.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a group or set of five, the same thing as a quintet.

clue.text: Qualification is framed by university official? No way

indicators.note: a framed thing sits within its frame, so is goes inside
no tells us to remove the abbreviation for way

parts.note: a provost heads some colleges
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A qualification is set by a university official, who refuses to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' drops ST (street, a way) from PROVOST to give PROVO; 'is framed by' puts IS in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition or qualification attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Close to destination, we turned left in town

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
turned means the word is faced the other way

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Nearing the end of a journey, we turned left into a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' takes N from destination; 'turned' makes EW from WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Newport is a town, in Wales and elsewhere, so the definition names its category.

clue.text: Not entirely convinced about the heart of Dali being so?

definitions.text: Not entirely convinced about the heart of Dali being so?

indicators.note: not entirely tells us to cut the word's last letter

parts.note: convinced means sure
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the heart means the middle letters

explanation.surface: Doubting what lies at the core of Salvador Dali's art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts SURE to SUR; 'the heart of' takes AL from DALI. Dali was a Surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dali's art was dreamlike and bizarre, the very quality of the Surrealist movement.

clue.text: Catch one who's not at home?

definitions.meaning: to land a fish by pulling it from a river is literally what the phrase says

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb phrase it means to catch by pulling from a river; as a noun phrase it is the idiom for someone out of their element.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a person ill at ease in strange surroundings, and literally it describes landing a catch.

clue.text: A bit unwell, I'm perhaps lacking in energy

indicators.note: a bit of the words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Someone a bit poorly, admitting they may be low on energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit' takes the letters running across unwELL I'M Perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means drooping and without vigour, so lacking in energy is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Capacity one has to limit rise of Rome

parts.note: cap. is a dictionary abbreviation for capacity
the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written
a line is a limit or boundary, as in drawing the line

explanation.surface: A clue about how much power can curb the ascent of the Roman Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' means a hill: the Capitoline is one of the seven hills of Rome. 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of Rome's seven hills, and a hill is a rise in the ground.

clue.text: Article in French newspaper that is socialist

parts.note: le is the French definite article
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A piece in a French paper turns out to be left-wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftie is a colloquial term for someone on the political left, such as a socialist.

clue.text: See bird — cuckoo — shortly before end of April

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: cuckoo means crazy, dotty
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of April

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is told to look out for a cuckoo just before April ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts DOTTY to DOTT. 'cuckoo' looks like the bird, but it means crazy; 'See' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The dotterel is a small plover, a bird of mountain tops and tundra.
